svg.title: A fictional text thread from a fake bank fraud department, with three warning signs marked
svg.desc: A made-up text thread from "Bank Fraud Dept.": an alert about a $1,240 charge asks for a YES or NO reply; after a NO, the messages say a fraud specialist will call and not to hang up (warning sign 1, pressure to act now), to move money to a safe account by sending it by Zelle to yourself at their number (sign 2: a real bank never asks this), and not to tell anyone at the branch (sign 3, secrecy, even from your own bank). The safe move: hang up and call the number on the back of your card.
svg.text: FICTIONAL · FOR ILLUSTRATION
Bank Fraud Dept.
Text message
ALERT: A $1,240 charge was
attempted on your card. Reply YES
if this was you, NO if not.
NO
A fraud specialist will call you
now. Stay on the line. Don't hang
up.
To protect your money, move it to
a safe account. Send it by Zelle
to yourself at this number.
Don't tell anyone at the branch.
They may be part of the fraud.
Pressure to act now, before you can check.
"Move your money to keep it safe." A real
bank never asks this.
Secrecy, even from your own bank.
Hang up and call the number on the back of
your card.
